currentContext.business: Mphasis is an information technology solutions provider that leverages next-generation technologies and AI capabilities to help global enterprises transform their businesses, leading with design and architecture and blending deep domain expertise with technology. It delivers Application Services (design and development of customised software applications, plus maintenance, enhancement and testing of customer-developed and third-party software), Business Process Services (customer service, transaction processing and compliance knowledge processing, including transformation and integration of processes using automation tools) and Infrastructure Services (end-to-end managed mobility, workplace management, hosting, data centre, payment managed solutions and help desk). The company goes to market through a tribes-led, competency-based model and its Mphasis.ai platform family, serving Banking and Financial Services, Insurance, Technology/Media/Telecom and Logistics & Transportation clients, with the Americas as its prime market.

Application Services: Design and development of customised software applications
Maintenance, enhancement and testing of customer-developed and third-party software
Business Process Services: Process transformation and integration using automation tools
AI platforms and IP: Continuum AI™ (via Theory and Practice acquisition)

currentContext.expansion: The routed sections disclose no physical capex programme, plant, delivery-centre count or capacity addition — as an asset-light IT services business, Mphasis frames expansion as platform build-out, capability acquisition and partnerships. The principal build-out described is the AI platform stack: Mphasis introduced Mphasis NeoIP™ during the year, an AI-powered platform that integrates multiple Mphasis.ai solutions and orchestrates agentic solutions across Modernization, Application Development, IT Operations, Business Operations, Engineering and AI Governance, built on the earlier NeoCrux™ and NeoZeta™ platforms launched the prior year and with Mphasis Ontosphere at its core. Management describes the launch of Mphasis Tria, its Enterprise Agency Platform, as 'the culmination of years of investment in AI, including Mphasis NeoIP™, enterprise intelligence, orchestration and transformation', with Mphasis Modernize™ and Mphasis Optimize™ translating this into structured programmes with clear milestones. Inorganic expansion is limited to the acquisition of Theory and Practice and its Continuum AI™ platform, which the company says strengthens its decision-intelligence capability, alongside strategic partnerships with Sixfold and Aokah. On the physical footprint, the only disclosure is environmental efficiency of existing facilities — 23% of facilities have achieved LEED Platinum certification and three locations hold 5-Star ratings from India's Bureau of Energy Efficiency. No capex amount, commissioning date, site name, headcount-capacity target or ramp timeline is stated anywhere in the routed text.

risks.risk: Geographic concentration in the Americas / export dependence
risks.note: Management states 'Americas is our prime market, and this geography contributed 83.5% of our revenues in FY26', and the BRSR discloses that 'Mphasis Limited's export sales percentage is 90% for FY26'. A demand, policy or tariff shock in the United States therefore transmits almost directly to the top line; the Board's Report flags that trade tariffs and macroeconomic uncertainty are already prompting enterprises to scrutinise technology spending more carefully.

risks.risk: Vertical concentration in Banking, Financial Services and Insurance
risks.note: The MD&A states 'Banking and Financial Services and Insurance segments comprise 67.0% of our overall revenue', with BFS the declared focus vertical. Two-thirds of revenue is exposed to a single macro-sensitive client industry whose technology budgets tighten with credit conditions — which the MD&A notes are among the channels through which the Middle East conflict is introducing uncertainty.

The BRSR discloses that 100% of turnover comes from a single main activity — computer programming activities (IT consultancy, information and communication services). There is no diversifying business line to offset a downturn in enterprise IT services demand.

The MD&A states the global economy is 'entering a period of elevated and broadening risks', with OECD projecting global GDP growth slowing from 3.2% in 2025 to 2.9% in 2026 and the escalation of the Middle East conflict entirely negating earlier upward revisions, creating uncertainty across supply chains, commodity prices and credit conditions. It cites McKinsey's March 2026 outlook noting geopolitical instability 'is now the most-cited threat to enterprise growth'.

Reported growth is materially inflated by currency: 'During the year Indian Rupee depreciated 5.3% against USD. Adjusting for the Rupee depreciation, overall gross revenue grew 6.7% in FY26' versus 12.6% reported. The Results of Operations table also carries a 'Profit / (loss) on cash flow hedges reclassified to revenue' line, indicating hedging exposure between gross and net revenue.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the AI-led transformation thesis
risks.note: The Board's Report concedes that 'the path from potential to value is harder than it looks' — most enterprise AI investment is stalled at the information-processing layer, enterprises struggle to organise information for AI, and 'most such programmes stall or fail before they deliver value'. Mphasis' AI-led pipeline and platform investments (Tria, NeoIP, Ontosphere) are underwritten by clients successfully crossing that gap; management also frames a competitive fault line between 'companies that service AI' and 'companies that deploy it'.

risks.risk: Structurally declining legacy revenue pools and channel de-risking
risks.note: The company is deliberately shrinking its DXC channel ('We continue to de-risk DXC business, the revenues from which declined 14.8%'), while Infrastructure Services revenue declined and Logistics & Transportation fell sharply as a share of the business. Growth therefore depends entirely on new-customer ramp-ups and wallet-share gains in the Direct business offsetting these run-offs.

The MD&A notes industry-wide changes in labour composition and reliance on 'large-scale upskilling of the workforce in AI', while the FY26 P&L carried an exceptional item described as 'towards impact of change in labour laws' — evidencing that statutory employment-cost changes flow directly to the company. Cost of revenues is dominated by direct people costs, so wage and utilisation dynamics drive margin.

one-line thesis: Q1 is a foundation quarter — revenue $471 mn, +2.1% QoQ and +8.3% YoY in constant currency, with margin down 60 bps on deal-ramp costs and the TAP acquisition earn-out. The signal is the pipeline: 2.8x since the Mphasis.ai launch and at an all-time high, with AI-led deals now 70% of it, and the newly launched Tria platform closing multiple opportunities within seven weeks. Management guided Q2 to "the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years" while holding the FY27 range and margin band unchanged.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > Margin walk: TAP acquisition impact ~0.35% — structured so roughly two-thirds of potential consideration is earn-out flowing entirely through the P&L (not purchase accounting), so it recurs over the next couple of years. The second driver was a steep utilisation drop taken deliberately in anticipation of Q2 growth; that one reverses. Hedge losses: cumulative OCI hedge losses down ~INR 50 cr between March and June; expected to trend down but "will take a couple of quarters" and "will improve but not go away fully." Segment/geo: Americas +3.9% QoQ / +11.4% YoY Direct; ROW +6.1% QoQ (GCC-led); EMEA optically hit by revenue moving geographies on a globally structured deal. BFS +9.4% YoY / +0.8% QoQ (8 straight quarters at >3.5% compound quarterly growth); Insurance +17.8% YoY but −3.1% QoQ after four strong quarters; TMT +16.4% QoQ / +13.6% YoY; BPO +12.7% QoQ / +14% YoY; Enterprise Applications +11.9% YoY; Others +5.2% QoQ. Three large deals closed including one over $100 mn; 63% of Q1 TCV wins were AI-led.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Revenue growth: FY27 maintained at high single-digit to low double-digit growth in constant currency, "despite the uncertain macro environment." Red Oak is already baked into this range.
Q2 specifically: "Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years."
Margin: FY27 EBIT within the band of 14.75% to 15.75% — "not because we are defending a floor, but because we are making deliberate platform investments while holding financial discipline."

Cash conversion: operating cash flow conversion expected to remain at 80% of net income through FY27, with normalisation of the OCF/EBITDA ratio from FY28 as upfront investments in large deals begin to be recovered.
DSO: to improve progressively through the remainder of the year.
Red Oak: consummation expected end of August / early September 2026 — contract assignment and employee takeover in progress; will not carry a full-quarter impact in Q2.
Insurance margin: transformation-programme ramp costs to normalise over the next two quarters.
order book & pipeline: Total pipeline grew 8% sequentially and 28% YoY to an all-time high, and is 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch. Composition: non-BFS pipeline +18% QoQ; large deals (>$20 mn) pipeline +10% QoQ; BFS pipeline +100% YoY. AI-led deals have gone from 12% to 70% of pipeline and are "now stabilizing" — management's read is that AI is no longer a deal type but the way the company competes across all verticals and sizes. Modernization and Everything-as-a-Platform are the fastest-growing solution archetypes, mapping directly to the newly launched product lines. The TTM TCV-to-revenue correlation fell from >0.9 to ~0.74, which management explained as a feature: short-burst, deployment-led deals consume within one or two quarters, and foundation-building work completes in 12–16 weeks before scale deployment waves follow.
segment / subsidiary detail: BFS: stable, eight quarters of structural growth, compound quarterly growth over 3.5% — described as the strongest among peers.
Insurance: grew ~35% in FY26; the sequential dip reflects project milestone completions, not client loss — "We have no client impact to call out as we stand." Expected to be a key FY27 growth driver.

Logistics & Transportation: genuinely headwinded by macro and geopolitics; now a small unit where "small number changes drive high percentage variations." More work to be done here and in Airlines and Railroads.
TMT: returned to strong growth as recent deal wins ramped.

Customer-contract acquisitions (OKIN, Red Oak): these are vendor-consolidation deals, not M&A — no entity is taken over, but the accounting follows acquisition accounting with the consideration almost entirely customer relationships and intangibles. Typical consideration is 1x–1.2x revenue. OKIN delivered close to $4 mn of revenue in Q1 against a total contract value including contingent consideration of $5.5 mn — i.e. it already outgrew the original LOI assumption.
growth verticals / optionality: The platform thesis rests on Tria: Modernize builds "enterprise memory" by extracting structured context from systems, rules, workflows and process history; Optimize then uses that memory to improve decision loops across revenue, pricing, demand, supply chain and risk. The commercial consequence management is pointing at is revenue quality — ARR and managed services now being bundled together in Tria deals, Tria influencing large deals at the evaluation stage as a proof point, and new addressable penetration at existing clients opening budget pools that were inaccessible under the service-led model. The FDE (forward deployed engineer) motion is small pods of 3–5 elite engineers at high billing rates whose job is to deliver proof of value and hand over to scale delivery — management was explicit that the value is the platform deployment and subsequent managed-services stickiness, not the FDE margin itself.
6a. moat & competitive position: A defined "right to win" at a specific intersection: "this problem sits at the intersection of brownfield enterprise complexity, integration depth, domain-specific decision intelligence, and governance — precisely the territory we have built over thirty years. Not many AI-native startups can replicate that context. Not many hyperscalers want to own that accountability."

Refusal to compete on price: "we are not competing on price because that's a game that we really don't want to play… that price discounting game only works when you're doing effort-based pricing. But when you change the equation and do outcome-based pricing, it really doesn't make any sense for clients to look at it that way."
Demand compression as evidence: "within seven weeks of platform launch, multiple opportunities moved from conversation to closure and are now moving to execution. That is not a normal sales cycle."
BFS depth: eight consecutive quarters of >3.5% compound quarterly growth, and 100% YoY BFS pipeline growth, in a period when peers report BFS caution.
margins & cost dynamics: Two identifiable drags this quarter, one recurring and one reversing. themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
